title: Foundations: pnpm workspace, shared contracts, CLI boundaries, and CI
body:
> Historical foundation issue scope. Current serving uses a Docker gateway and offline Linux ARM64 CPU worker; prepaid Solana devnet USDC is implemented alongside TEST_CREDIT regression accounting. See `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/docker-sandbox.md` and `docs/payments.md`. The original scope below is retained for traceability, not current product status.

## Outcome

Set up the shared base so the provider, buyer, cloud, and frontend lanes can work independently. This issue belongs to the foundation team. Record the exact delivered baseline in the closing PR; scaffolding does not imply production features are complete.

## Ownership and scope

Lane: **Foundation owners**.

Own workspace tooling, the existing Next.js application upgrade, shared contract baseline, external MCPWire CLI adapter baseline, provider startup skeleton, Volcano health-function scaffold, CI, and repository documentation. Domain completion and actual cloud deployment belong to the follow-up issues.

## Dependencies

- None; this is the shared prerequisite.

Mock/fake boundaries may support isolated development while prerequisites are in progress, but do not count as completed integration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pin the pnpm package manager and current supported stable framework/tooling versions; retain one committed pnpm lockfile.
- [ ] Provide consistent build, lint, typecheck, and test scripts and CI on pull requests.
- [ ] Add versioned shared schemas and meaningful validation tests for initial provider, quote, and request contracts.
- [ ] Add the external MCPWire CLI invocation boundary without importing internal MCPWire modules.
- [ ] Add the macOS launch-check/provider scaffold and a Volcano health-function scaffold with clear implemented-versus-planned behavior.
- [ ] Document component ownership, local setup, environment requirements, team dependencies, and deployment readiness without claiming a cloud deployment occurred.

## Validation

Run clean pnpm install from the lockfile, repository checks, and production web build. Include schema-invalid-input checks and CLI boundary tests. Link check output in the foundation PR.

## Shared decisions

Follow `docs/architecture.md`, the PRD, and `AGENTS.md`. Target macOS/Apple Silicon, native Ollama, fixed request prices, agent-first discovery, external MCPWire, and Volcano. Changes to shared schemas, lifecycle policy, or component ownership require coordination with consuming lanes.

title: Provider: implement macOS capability tests and persistent inference daemon
body:
> Historical foundation issue scope. Current serving uses a Docker gateway and offline Linux ARM64 CPU worker; prepaid Solana devnet USDC is implemented alongside TEST_CREDIT regression accounting. See `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/docker-sandbox.md` and `docs/payments.md`. The original scope below is retained for traceability, not current product status.

## Outcome

A provider Mac becomes discoverable only after a fresh launch suite verifies that it can execute the advertised bounded inference profile.

## Ownership and scope

Lane: **Provider lane**.

Own persistent provider daemon, dedicated native Ollama supervision, approved model setup, local request queue/admission, startup reports, and wake/failure readiness invalidation. Extend the shared capability contracts through review. Do not put worker state in disposable per-peer MCP adapters.

## Dependencies

- [Foundations: pnpm workspace, shared contracts, CLI boundaries, and CI](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/1)

Mock/fake boundaries may support isolated development while prerequisites are in progress, but do not count as completed integration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Use macOS on Apple Silicon and a pinned small approved model, initially qwen2.5:0.5b; make model download an explicit setup action.
- [ ] Check runtime/model identity, memory/disk prerequisites, model load, smoke generation, output cap, timeout/cancellation, and loopback exposure.
- [ ] Generate a versioned startup report; failed checks remain unavailable, and local success alone marks peer connectivity unverified.
- [ ] Enforce one active request, queue depth two, context/output/deadline profile, and provider pause/drain/emergency-stop controls across all peers.
- [ ] Retest after wake or model/runtime change; heartbeat publication is gated on passing the fresh report.
- [ ] Persist request terminal state and encrypted retrievable results before acknowledging completion; support reconnect retrieval and retention cleanup.

## Validation

Run against a supported Mac with the real model plus injectable failure fixtures. Verify missing model, unsupported host, runtime crash, timeout, cancellation, sleep/wake, and two peers sharing one concurrency limit. Record measured profile limits.

## Shared decisions

Follow `docs/architecture.md`, the PRD, and `AGENTS.md`. Target macOS/Apple Silicon, native Ollama, fixed request prices, agent-first discovery, external MCPWire, and Volcano. Changes to shared schemas, lifecycle policy, or component ownership require coordination with consuming lanes.

## Outcome

Provider and buyer components use the external MCPWire CLI reliably without a fork or internal module imports.

## Ownership and scope

Lane: **Transport lane**.

Own packages/mcpwire lifecycle behavior: pinned executable resolution, command construction, noninteractive readiness/ticket capture, MCP stdio bridging, restarts, cleanup, and diagnostics. Exclude payments, registry, model execution, and generic agent tool routing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Capture private readiness/ticket output without leaking it into application logs or public responses; isolate any format-dependent parser.
- [ ] Expose typed ready, failed, closed, and timeout outcomes; terminate child process trees predictably on shutdown.
- [ ] Test the per-peer MCP child lifecycle and prove the application daemon survives disposable child disconnects.
- [ ] Handle ticket rotation/restart and prevent silent replay of uncertain tool calls.
- [ ] Provide a separate-peer probe used by provider readiness, including an explicit unverified state when a probe cannot run.
- [ ] Validate argument-preview logging against the application authentication envelope and document any upstream gap requiring a separate change.

title: Registry: live provider discovery API and MCP tools on Volcano
body:
> Historical foundation issue scope. Current serving uses a Docker gateway and offline Linux ARM64 CPU worker; prepaid Solana devnet USDC is implemented alongside TEST_CREDIT regression accounting. See `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/docker-sandbox.md` and `docs/payments.md`. The original scope below is retained for traceability, not current product status.

## Outcome

Buyer agents can query fresh, compatible providers through structured discovery tools without visiting the public website.

## Ownership and scope

Lane: **Control-plane lane**.

Own durable provider/capability registry, authenticated registration and heartbeats, readiness queries, discover_providers/get_provider tools, and machine-readable errors. Use the same service layer for API and MCP. The public site consumes a safe projection; purchase accounting is separate.

## Dependencies

- [Foundations: pnpm workspace, shared contracts, CLI boundaries, and CI](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/1)

Mock/fake boundaries may support isolated development while prerequisites are in progress, but do not count as completed integration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Store versioned provider/model/profile reports, price references, startup IDs, test timestamps, and heartbeat expiry in durable storage.
- [ ] Accept registration/heartbeats only for authorized prototype providers and reject reports that claim readiness without required evidence.
- [ ] Implement ready-only filtering by capability/model, request bounds, fixed-price ceiling, and observed latency with stable pagination.
- [ ] Use initial 15-second heartbeat and 45-second expiry defaults; stale or failed providers cannot appear ready even if cleanup jobs lag.
- [ ] Return typed freshness and readiness reasons without prompt data, private tickets, device serials, precise location, or buyer activity.
- [ ] Expose discovery MCP transport/authentication using supported Volcano deployment primitives and publish a tested client example.

## Validation

Test expiry with a controlled clock, invalid/out-of-order reports, duplicate heartbeats, filtering, and safe public projection. Run an MCP client discovery test against the deployed test environment when deployment support is available.

## Shared decisions

Follow `docs/architecture.md`, the PRD, and `AGENTS.md`. Target macOS/Apple Silicon, native Ollama, fixed request prices, agent-first discovery, external MCPWire, and Volcano. Changes to shared schemas, lifecycle policy, or component ownership require coordination with consuming lanes.

title: Accounting: fixed quotes, atomic test-credit reservations, and receipts
body:
> Historical foundation issue scope. Current serving uses a Docker gateway and offline Linux ARM64 CPU worker; prepaid Solana devnet USDC is implemented alongside TEST_CREDIT regression accounting. See `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/docker-sandbox.md` and `docs/payments.md`. The original scope below is retained for traceability, not current product status.

## Outcome

A buyer reserves a known fixed total before execution and is charged at most once for a durably completed bounded request.

## Ownership and scope

Lane: **Accounting lane**.

Own versioned quote service, integer-unit test-credit balances, owner spending policies, atomic reservations, balanced ledger entries, settlement/release/refund, and reconciliation. Real blockchain funding and payouts are outside this prototype issue.

## Dependencies

- [Foundations: pnpm workspace, shared contracts, CLI boundaries, and CI](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/1)
- [Registry: live provider discovery API and MCP tools on Volcano](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/4)

Mock/fake boundaries may support isolated development while prerequisites are in progress, but do not count as completed integration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Quotes bind provider/model/profile, immutable fixed price and all fees, expiry, request bounds, and failure/cancellation policy.
- [ ] Concurrent purchases cannot overspend per-request, session, daily, or available-balance limits; buyer agents cannot increase owner authority.
- [ ] Use idempotency keys across purchase, reservation, completion events, settlement, and refund.
- [ ] Settle one fixed total for successful durable completion regardless of token counts; release failed/rejected/cancelled work.
- [ ] Resolve completion-versus-cancellation through a single durable terminal-state decision.
- [ ] Keep uncertain outcomes pending reconciliation without replay or duplicate debit, with an explicit deadline and operator outcome.
- [ ] Issue receipts reconciling buyer debit, provider earnings, and fees; use compensating entries for refunds.

## Validation

Use real transactional database integration tests for competing reservations, duplicate callbacks, cancellation races, unavailable provider, crash/reconnect, and balanced ledger invariants. Confirm no real-money integration is enabled.

## Shared decisions

Follow `docs/architecture.md`, the PRD, and `AGENTS.md`. Target macOS/Apple Silicon, native Ollama, fixed request prices, agent-first discovery, external MCPWire, and Volcano. Changes to shared schemas, lifecycle policy, or component ownership require coordination with consuming lanes.

title: Host MCP: buyer-bound authorization and daemon-backed inference tools
body:
> Historical foundation issue scope. Current serving uses a Docker gateway and offline Linux ARM64 CPU worker; prepaid Solana devnet USDC is implemented alongside TEST_CREDIT regression accounting. See `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/docker-sandbox.md` and `docs/payments.md`. The original scope below is retained for traceability, not current product status.

## Outcome

A disposable provider MCP server exposes only approved inference operations and cannot execute paid work from a copied connectivity ticket alone.

## Ownership and scope

Lane: **Host/auth lane**.

Own provider MCP tool schemas/handlers, restricted local daemon IPC, entitlement verification, buyer proof-of-key possession, expected-provider response binding, replay protection, and session envelope. Platform signing integration must share reviewed contracts with accounting. Do not duplicate model workers or device limits in the adapter.

## Dependencies

- [Foundations: pnpm workspace, shared contracts, CLI boundaries, and CI](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/1)
- [Provider: implement macOS capability tests and persistent inference daemon](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/2)
- [Accounting: fixed quotes, atomic test-credit reservations, and receipts](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/5)
- [Transport: supervise external MCPWire share/join lifecycle](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/3)

Mock/fake boundaries may support isolated development while prerequisites are in progress, but do not count as completed integration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Expose get_capabilities, run_inference, get_request, and cancel_request with strict validation and typed errors.
- [ ] Bind authorization to buyer/provider keys, startup/session, quote, request, operation, payload digest, expiry, limits, and reserved amount.
- [ ] Verify identity at the application layer rather than assuming the MCPWire child receives the transport peer identity.
- [ ] Reject copied-ticket-only, expired, wrong-buyer, wrong-provider, altered-payload, stale-startup, and replay attempts before inference.
- [ ] Restrict IPC and runtime endpoints so alternate methods/resources/prompts cannot bypass paid admission.
- [ ] Keep logs free of raw authorization secrets and prompts; test actual MCPWire argument-preview behavior.
- [ ] Keep requests retrievable after a per-peer child exits and prevent a new peer from gaining access to another buyer result.

## Validation

Test negative authorization cases and payload tampering through real MCP calls, two-peer concurrency, adapter death, reconnect retrieval, and local endpoint access control. Review the signing/canonicalization design before publishing an authentication contract.

## Shared decisions

Follow `docs/architecture.md`, the PRD, and `AGENTS.md`. Target macOS/Apple Silicon, native Ollama, fixed request prices, agent-first discovery, external MCPWire, and Volcano. Changes to shared schemas, lifecycle policy, or component ownership require coordination with consuming lanes.

title: Buyer MCP: automatic discovery-to-inference provider handoff
body:
> Historical foundation issue scope. Current serving uses a Docker gateway and offline Linux ARM64 CPU worker; prepaid Solana devnet USDC is implemented alongside TEST_CREDIT regression accounting. See `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/docker-sandbox.md` and `docs/payments.md`. The original scope below is retained for traceability, not current product status.

## Outcome

A buyer agent uses one stable MCP facade to discover, quote, purchase, execute, cancel, and retrieve inference across providers without reconfiguring its MCP client.

## Ownership and scope

Lane: **Buyer lane**.

Own local buyer MCP tools, cloud service client, owner-policy configuration, private connection handoff, signed request envelopes, MCPWire join client sessions, and receipt presentation. Treat provider descriptions and model results as data. Do not implement cloud ledger rules in the buyer.

## Dependencies

- [Foundations: pnpm workspace, shared contracts, CLI boundaries, and CI](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/1)
- [Registry: live provider discovery API and MCP tools on Volcano](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/4)
- [Accounting: fixed quotes, atomic test-credit reservations, and receipts](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/5)
- [Transport: supervise external MCPWire share/join lifecycle](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/3)
- [Host MCP: buyer-bound authorization and daemon-backed inference tools](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/6)

Mock/fake boundaries may support isolated development while prerequisites are in progress, but do not count as completed integration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Provide structured discover_providers, get_provider, quote_inference, purchase_access, run_inference, get_request, and cancel_request tools.
- [ ] Check accepted quote against owner-authorized budgets before purchase; do not permit a model to increase authority.
- [ ] Connect through the transport package and invoke provider tools without dynamic MCP server installation per purchase.
- [ ] Bind signed operations to the accepted provider/request/envelope and verify provider response identity.
- [ ] Handle stale discovery, unavailable capacity, expired quote, peer disconnect, cancelled work, and pending reconciliation with typed agent-facing outcomes.
- [ ] Reuse request IDs on retry and retrieve known state rather than automatically rerunning uncertain work.
- [ ] Return fixed charge, finish reason, diagnostic usage, and receipt reference; keep tickets/private grants out of agent-visible logs.

## Validation

Drive the facade with an MCP test client through mocked boundary failures, then a real provider. Verify no manual server reconfiguration during provider changes and no double execution after reconnect.

## Shared decisions

Follow `docs/architecture.md`, the PRD, and `AGENTS.md`. Target macOS/Apple Silicon, native Ollama, fixed request prices, agent-first discovery, external MCPWire, and Volcano. Changes to shared schemas, lifecycle policy, or component ownership require coordination with consuming lanes.

title: Integration: two-Mac agent demo and transaction failure matrix
body:
> Historical foundation issue scope. Current serving uses a Docker gateway and offline Linux ARM64 CPU worker; prepaid Solana devnet USDC is implemented alongside TEST_CREDIT regression accounting. See `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/docker-sandbox.md` and `docs/payments.md`. The original scope below is retained for traceability, not current product status.

## Outcome

Prove the product end to end: a buyer agent discovers two Macs, selects an eligible provider, completes one fixed-price inference through MCPWire, and retrieves matching results and receipt state.

## Ownership and scope

Lane: **Integration lane**.

Own cross-component integration harness, documented hardware setup, real agent/MCP client demo, failure injection, and release evidence. Keep deterministic unit/contract tests in their owning packages and add integration coverage for seams rather than duplicating them.

## Dependencies

- [Provider: implement macOS capability tests and persistent inference daemon](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/2)
- [Transport: supervise external MCPWire share/join lifecycle](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/3)
- [Registry: live provider discovery API and MCP tools on Volcano](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/4)
- [Accounting: fixed quotes, atomic test-credit reservations, and receipts](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/5)
- [Host MCP: buyer-bound authorization and daemon-backed inference tools](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/6)
- [Buyer MCP: automatic discovery-to-inference provider handoff](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/7)
- [Volcano: deploy control plane, discovery interface, and frontend](https://github.com/carlosrivera/panas/issues/9)

Mock/fake boundaries may support isolated development while prerequisites are in progress, but do not count as completed integration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Run capability tests at launch for both Macs and publish only verified eligible providers.
- [ ] Discover and choose by compatibility, bounds, price, readiness, and freshness without website interaction or per-provider client reconfiguration.
- [ ] Execute via MCPWire with expected buyer/provider identities and reconcile one fixed charge with provider earnings and fees.
- [ ] Exercise copied tickets, expired/altered authorization, duplicate purchases, concurrent spending, queue overflow, and request replay.
- [ ] Exercise cancellation/completion races, deadline, provider crash, adapter disconnect, sleep/wake, and unavailable Volcano services.
- [ ] Prove reconnect retrieves original state/result and no failure path automatically creates duplicate execution/debit.
- [ ] Publish reproducible commands, measured timings, known limits, and a failure-result matrix; report blockers rather than substituting mocked results for hardware/cloud proof.

## Validation

Use two physical supported Macs, the actual pinned model/MCPWire release, the deployed test control plane, and a buyer MCP client. Verify ledger/receipt invariants and redact all secrets from retained evidence.

## Shared decisions

Follow `docs/architecture.md`, the PRD, and `AGENTS.md`. Target macOS/Apple Silicon, native Ollama, fixed request prices, agent-first discovery, external MCPWire, and Volcano. Changes to shared schemas, lifecycle policy, or component ownership require coordination with consuming lanes.
